MN202611_evto7ppnlf.t:
Rainbow laces were a common sight for several years across football and other sports

Warning: this article contains offensive language

Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with new data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?

Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a new LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.

The lowkey launch contrasts with the landscape of a few years ago, when England internationals like Jordan Henderson and Conor Coady were proudly proclaiming their allyship.

"The one thing it [Premier League With Pride last season] was lacking was engagement from players," said Jon Holmes, founder and lead of news organisation and campaign group Sports Media LGBT.

"Not only would you have the rainbow armbands, but clearer allyship from players - that was more around the late 2010s. That has been in decline."

A report last month from anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out says they received a new high of 1,744 discrimination reports during the 2025-26 season, a 25% increase on the previous campaign. In this, reports of homophobia rose 46% to 203.

Kick It Out said it had received 142 reports of discriminatory mass chanting during the season, a 41% increase on 2024-25 and the highest number recorded. These reports included increases in homophobic and transphobic chants.

A prime example is the 'rent boy' chant predominantly aimed at Chelsea players and fans, for which incidents had dropped since it was criminalised in 2022. However, the combined 24 reports of homophobic chanting in 2025-26 season were the most in three years.

According to Kick It Out, , external many of the incidents over the past few seasons can be linked to domestic and world events, such as the Supreme Court ruling on gender leading to the FA's ban on transgender women in the women's game, which it says led to a spike in transphobic abuse.

The first Premier League With Pride event included rainbow branding at grounds - but nothing involving players

BBC Sport asked all 20 Premier League clubs what diversity policies they have regarding the LGBTQ+ community, and how much of their budget is dedicated to such schemes.

Nine clubs responded to the BBC request. None said how much money they invest in these areas.

A Nottingham Forest spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The club commits significant funding to this important area, and has an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion lead whose role is dedicated to ensuring inclusion is at the heart of everything we do."

Some clubs do visibly engage with their local LGBTQ+ community. Leeds United have been a sponsor of the city's Pride celebrations since 2018. Luke Ayling, then Leeds captain, marched in the Pride parade in 2022.

Brighton are annually represented in their city's extensive Pride events, as are the Manchester clubs.

Manchester City host an annual Progress flag-raising ceremony, while Manchester United said staff marched in the city centre parade. They also ran a flag competition with LGBTQ+ supporters' club Rainbow Devils, with the winning design displayed at Old Trafford for all matchdays.

Tottenham said that at the start of 2024, Spurs in the Community helped launch a weekly football session for members of the LGBTQ+ community.

And for the first time this season, all 20 current Premier League clubs have dedicated fan groups for LGBTQ+ supporters.

"It feels like there is a renaissance in the LGBT fan movement," said Holmes. "There is a rise in homophobia, but it does seem like the authorities are sitting up and taking notice. We can feel a degree of optimism."

But it is difficult for Premier League teams to encourage LGBTQ+ allyship and diversity, when representation within clubs is a mixed bag at best.

According to Kick It Out, which gathered data on the senior management teams from 17 out of the 20 current Premier League clubs, just 0.3% of people in those roles openly identify as LGBTQ+ - well below the UK population average according to latest national census data, with 4% of the British population identifying as LGBTQ+.

At a senior coaching level, from 11 clubs which responded there is no-one from the LGBTQ+ community.

Kick It Out says, comparing the dataset to relevant census data, that if true diversity in football's workforce were to be achieved, over 100 more people from the LGBTQ+ community would have to be employed at Premier League clubs.

The Premier League previously had a high profile association with LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall's Rainbow Laces campaign - but this was ended before the 2025-26 season

Rainbow Laces started in 2014-15 as a collaboration between Stonewall, Paddy Power and the Premier League. For two game weeks, usually around the end of November, players would wear rainbow-coloured laces or armbands, and the colourful branding would be seen in grounds and on broadcast idents.

Holmes said by the end it was doing more harm than good.

"I think the novelty of Rainbow Laces wore off," he told BBC Sport. "It also became more newsworthy to talk about the controversies; it became more difficult for players to engage without difficult questions.

"Also, club media departments are more risk averse, given growing toxicity on social media.

"It has been misconstrued that players were forced to engage, I think it was because Rainbow Laces became de rigueur, and it was perceived that captains would need to lead with the armband and allyship."

Rainbow armbands were introduced in 2017 for captains, having first been worn by MLS club Orlando City following the mass shooting at Pulse, an LGBTQ+ nightclub, in the city in 2016.

But the Premier League held its final Rainbow Laces campaign from 29 November to 5 December, 2024, and it was surrounded by controversy.

Marc Guehi, then Crystal Palace captain, wrote 'I Love Jesus' on his armband in what was widely viewed as a protest against wearing the armband (which was not mandatory).

Ipswich captain Sam Morsy refused to wear the armband, while Manchester United scrapped plans for a Rainbow Laces-themed jacket during the pre-match ceremonies following an objection by Noussair Mazraoui.

Simon Blake, CEO of Stonewall, admitted to BBC Sport that by the end of its 12-year lifespan in the Premier League, Rainbow Laces in that form had run its course.

"When it started, getting a few people to wear the laces was success," he said. "When it ended, when a few people didn't wear them there was criticism.

"If a campaign no longer has a positive vibe, perhaps it is time to do something different.

"Everything must evolve and change, but visibility still matters, it is important not to throw the baby out with the bathwater."

Stonewall held its first ever Rainbow Laces Day on 8 October this year, to encourage LGBTQ+ people to engage with sport. It had no connection with the Premier League.

Marc Guehi and Crystal Palace did not face any action after he wrote on his rainbow armband

It is notable that the players most ardently against Rainbow Laces were also vocal in their religious beliefs.

Guehi has spoken of the importance in his life of his faith and was one of several devout Christian players in the Crystal Palace dressing room. Both Morsy and Mazraoui are practicing Muslims.

Both Holmes and Blake acknowledge that this may have had an impact on Rainbow Laces.

"The influence of religion is clearly quite significant, but I think more understanding is coming in too," said Holmes.

"We have seen many parts of life less willing to engage with Pride, and football reflects that. The nature of LGBT campaigns is peaks and troughs, and we are in a trough."

"We don't have any specific data about what people's beliefs and views are, but we are in a world where people have different views, even within religions themselves," added Blake.

"The important thing is about behaviours, and we must learn to live with people who have these different beliefs and respect them.

"I don't want to speculate, as it would be too easy to assume people of faith would not be inclusive, I know from my work across 30 years that is not true; I have worked with many religious people who are LGBTQ+ supportive. Freedom of belief is important."

The current picture is a difficult one for gay and trans people in football at all levels.

The grassroots game is where the bulk of the increase in abuse has occurred, says Kick It Out, which claims it received 140% more reports last year than in the 2024-25 season. Three quarters of these reports are from senior grassroots games, where the players are over 18.

Away from football, research by Stonewall published in October found 11% of LGBTQ+ people in the UK avoid the gym, exercise classes or sports groups for fear of discrimination. Among trans people, the figure rises to 29%.

It said 15% of LGBTQ+ people who had been to a live sporting event, or watched sport in a bar, in the past year had experienced discrimination there. This rose to 26% for trans people.

"What we know is that there is a lot of work going on around equality and diversity; we also know homophobia and transphobia continue to be rife," Blake said.

"We are in a world, whether at Premier League or grassroots football, where views that may have been perceived to be unacceptable are now being expressed freely. That influences peoples' relationship with sport."

Premier League With Pride will return in 2026-27.

"The matchday activations take place in February in line with LGBTQ+ History Month, when the league and clubs will showcase their commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion," a Premier League spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"There will be two match rounds dedicated to Premier League With Pride. This means all 20 clubs have a home game during that period, providing an opportunity to highlight and celebrate the LGBTQ+ community in football and showcase the work undertaken to make the game more inclusive.

"There is no centralised activation lined up for November."

The drugs agency described the seized package as a "potent strain of cannabis"

A basketball player from the US has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos.

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting to Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations.

The agency said an examination of the suspect's phone had pointed "to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity".

In statement on Sunday, the agency said he was arrested on Wednesday after airport officials noticed him abandoning his two checked-in bags and attempting to leave with his carry-on bag.

The two bags, which bore his name, contained 32 packs of the drug known as "Loud", a potent strain of cannabis, the agency said.

A tracking device was also recovered from the bags, the agency added.

The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player by the name Damonte Greene, with the most recent appearance at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand, on 26 September.

Nigeria, once regarded primarily as a transit hub for drug trafficking, has increasingly become a producer, consumer, and distributor of illegal drugs, according to the UN.

Recent NDLEA operations have uncovered several industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories, raising concerns about links between Nigerian drug producers and Mexican cartels seeking to manufacture and export the drug.

In September, the agency said it had dismantled a meth lab and arrested a Mexican suspected drug kingpin who was allegedly attempting to flee Nigeria through Lagos.

Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a highly addictive synthetic drug that can cause severe psychosis, heart attacks or stroke.

In August, a social media influencer suspected of links to an international drug trafficking network was arrested after the authorities seized cocaine worth nearly $28m (£21m), which was destined for the UK.

Alice Huang, ukekwaho kuba intasi y'Ubushinwa kandi wakundanye mu ibanga na Jensen Huang wahoze ayobora sosiyete ya Nvidia, yasezeye ku mwanya w'ubuyobozi muri sosiyete ya Megaspeed muri Kanama (8) mu 2025, nk'uko iyo sosiyete yabitangaje.

Ibi bitangajwe, mu gihe hakomeje ibibazo bivugwa kuri Nvidia nyuma y'amakuru yavugaga ko Jensen Huang yagiranye umubano wihariye na Alice Huang ndetse n'umwe mu bakozi b'iyo sosiyete ikora ibikoresho (chip) byifashishwa mu ikoranabuhanga ry'ubwenge buhangano (AI).

Megaspeed, sosiyete ifatwa nk'umuguzi mukuru wa chip za Nvidia muri Aziya y'Amajyepfo y'Iburasirazuba, ikaba ikomeje gutungwa agatoki ko yaba yaraguze Chips zakozwe na Nvidia mu buryo butemewe, binyuze mu mubano abayobozi b'ibigo byombi bari bafitanye.

Megaspeed yatangaje ko yatangije iperereza ryayo ryihariye, kuri ibyo birego birimo kuyivugwaho.

Yavuze ko raporo zigaruka ku bucuruzi bwayo, uruhererekane rw'itangwa ry'ibikoresho ndetse n'ibikorwa byayo ku rwego mpuzamahanga, zidafite ibimenyetso bifatika.

Yongeyeho ko ibikorwa byayo bikorwa mu buryo bwemewe n'amategeko kandi ko yashyizeho itsinda ry'abanyamategeko bo hanze y'icyo kigo, kugira ngo rikore iperereza ryimbitse.

Gusa ikigo cyo muri Amerika gisesengura ku bibazo by'umutekano, C4ADS, kivuga ko n'ubwo Alice Huang yari yaravuye ku buyobozi bwa Megaspeed, yakomeje kugira uruhare rukomeye mu mikorere yayo.

C4ADS yavuze ko Huang yakomeje kuba afite ijambo rikomeye muri sosiyete nyuma yo kuva ku buyobozi bwayo ku mugaragaro.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Muri Gashyantare(2) 2025, Alice Huang yakorewe iperereza n'abategetsi ba Singapore mu rwego rw'igenzura ryakorwaga kuri Megaspeed n'izindi sosiyete muri rusange.

Ku ruhande rwa Amerika, umudepite John Moolenaar yavuze ko Jensen Huang yemeye kuzitaba komite za Kongere zirimo gukora iperereza ku birego bifitanye isano n'u Bushinwa n'ikoranabuhanga rya AI.

Moolenaar yavuze ko ubwo buhamya buzafasha gusobanukirwa niba hari amakuru y'ibanga yaba yaratanzwe, n'uruhare uwo mugore ukekwaho ubutasi yaba yaragize ku byemezo bya Nvidia bijyanye n'ikoranabuhanga ry'ubwenge buhangano ndetse n'amabwiriza agenga iyoherezwa ryaryo mu mahanga.

Iki kibazo cyanakuruye impaka muri Washington, aho Minisitiri w'Imari wa Amerika Scott Bessent yasabye Nvidia gushaka umuyobozi mushya uturutse hanze y'iyo sosiyete.

Megaspeed ikekwaho gufasha ibigo byo mu Bushinwa kugera kuri chip zigezweho za Nvidia binyuze ku bigo byayo bibika kandi bigatunganya amakuru biri muri Maleziya, Indoneziya na Thailand.

Nvidia ntiyemerewe kugurisha chip zayo zigezweho mu Bushinwa bitewe n'amabwiriza ya Amerika agamije kugenzura iyoherezwa ry'ibikoresho by'ikoranabuhanga mu mahanga.

Megaspeed yavuze ko yubahiriza amategeko yose, harimo n'amabwiriza ya Amerika agenga iyoherezwa ry'ikoranabuhanga, ndetse n'amategeko y'ibihugu byose ikoreramo.

Ubushinwa bwo bwahakanye ko Alice Huang ari intasi, bunavuga ko Amerika itagomba gukoresha iki kibazo nk'urwitwazo rwo gukaza ibikorwa byo gukumira iterambere ry'ikoranabuhanga rya AI.

Kugeza ubu, Alice uvugwaho kuba imbarutso ya byose, ntaragira icyo atangaza ku mugaragaro.

Is Scotland's system limiting Ben Gannon-Doak's threat?

Two years ago, when Scotland defeated Croatia in the Nations League, that November night at Hampden was the dawn of Ben Gannon-Doak .

The then-teenager took £77m Manchester City man Josko Gvardiol to the cleaners and fans demanded the national team be built around the winger.

The Tartan Army's love for him has never faded - it arguably peaked when he stole the show in Scotland's World Cup opening win over Haiti - but it is fair to say they are growing frustrated, arguably on the Bournemouth man's behalf.

Under Sebastien Pocognoli, Gannon-Doak - who turned 21 on Wednesday - has been deployed at right wing-back, a role that demands defensive instincts unnatural to the pacy attacker.

It is already clear the new head coach is wedded to his preferred system, but it is one that is stifling one of Scotland's greatest attacking outlets - even though his final product still leaves a lot to be desired.

As his side prepare to visit Nations League Group B1 leaders Switzerland on Monday needing a win to have any chance of a promotion play-off place, Pocognoli has addressed both concerns - citing he is not uneasy about either - but pundits and punters alike cannot seem to shift their suspicions.

In that 1-0 victory over 10-man Croatia, it was Gannon-Doak's fearlessness in facing one of Europe's most elite and experienced teams that caught the eye.

His electric speed and directness excited a support who had long been crying out for a player with such qualities and the confidence in applying them. A natural winger, if you will.

In Pocognoli's system, though, there is no space for wingers. Something that former Rangers full-back Richard Foster says must "scunner" the wee man.

"When you're a full-back and you get to play wing-back, it's amazing - all of a sudden you are 10-20 yards up the pitch, doing more attacking and you can be a bit more aggressive," he said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"When you ask a winger to do that, most of the time they are absolutely scunnered. They are thinking 'I don't want to go back there'.

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"Looking at the squad [against North Macedonia], the three most exciting players we had - Findlay Curtis, Josh McPake and Gannon-Doak - are all wingers and he didn't bring two on.

"You look at the previous game [against Slovenia] and the difference McPake and Curtis made by coming on and taking players on - it gives everyone a lift.

"As a fan, you want to get excited about what you are watching. We are playing in a shape where we have the most exciting talents on the bench and they can't get on unless you adjust things. I just think he has to change the formation."

Foster is far from the only one wishing for a shift in shape - and not just for Gannon-Doak's benefit. Much has been made about the Scots' options in defence , too, and whether they match-up to the method.

However, it is arguable Gannon-Doak is the biggest casualty of them all.

"I don't think we're getting the best out of Ben," former Scotland captain Scott Brown told BBC Scotland.

"You saw him making so many last-ditch headers on Friday. He's having to add things to his game that he probably hasn't done before, like throw-ins, defending one-v-one."

No need to mention that throw-in, Scott. But that wasn't the only instance where Gannon-Doak looked a little lost. Think the 'Confused Travolta' meme.

While his position is a new worry, his precision with his final product is not.

Almost in a microcosm, Gannon-Doak's play was laid bare when be hurtled to the byeline before winning what turned out to be the match-winning penalty against the North Macedonians on Friday.

"He made a great run for the penalty, but I did think he could have got his shot away a bit earlier and maybe not taken that extra touch," Brown said.

Back in 2024, the wee live-wire was forgiven for not always finding a pal with a pass or choking at crunch time with his final ball.

However, as the years go on and the caps rack up, his shortcomings are still on show. His end product is still largely poor and patience is wearing thin.

"As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one-v-ones, I am happy," Pocognoli reiterated post his maiden Hampden win.

"With Ben, we know that he is a young age and needs to work on specific things. On Friday night, he had great opportunities.

"We know that he needs to improve on the end product. But he created a penalty and, against Slovenia and North Macedonia away, he created a number of unbelievable one-v-ones. He did that on Friday night as well.

"We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball.

So Pocognoli is comfortable for now. Already that appears to be a running theme for the head coach - even if others are not.

Highlights: Scotland 2-1 North Macedonia

Amatora y'umunyamabanga mukuru mushya w'umuryango w'ibihugu bivuga Igifaransa (Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie, OIF) yasubitsweho umwaka umwe, kubera kubura umukandida uhuriweho n'abanyamuryango, nkuko bitangazwa n'ibiro ntaramakuru AFP, bisubiramo amagambo y'abari hafi y'iyo dosiye, nyuma yuko inama ya OIF irangiye i Phnom Penh, mu murwa mukuru wa Cambodge.

Iyo nama yaranzwe n'ubushyamirane bukomeye hagati ya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) n'u Rwanda, bushingiye ku ntambara mu burasirazuba bwa RDC.

Umunyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo, wari umukandida ushaka manda ya gatatu, azaguma kuri uwo mwanya w'umunyamabanga mukuru wa OIF kugeza habaye andi matora, u Rwanda rutazagiramo umukandida, nkuko abo bavuganye na AFP babivuze.

Isubikwa ry'ayo matora ni bwo bwa mbere ribayeho mu mateka ya OIF, buri gihe yashyiragaho umunyamabanga mukuru wayo hagendewe ku mukandida uhuriweho na bose – Boutros Boutros Ghali, Abdou Diouf, Michaëlle Jean na Louise Mushikiwabo – kuva uwo mwanya washyirwaho mu mwaka wa 1997.

Abaterankunga ba mbere bakomeye ba OIF, ari bo Ubufaransa na Canada, basabye ko habaho ubumwe, ariko nta guhuriza ku mukandida umwe kwabayeho nyuma y'iminsi ibiri haba ibiganiro bikomeye mu muhezo i Phnom Penh, aho rwari rwabuze gica hagati ya RDC n'u Rwanda.

Kinshasa, ishinja u Rwanda gufasha umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa FRN – wahoze ari M23 – mu burasirazuba bw'icyo gihugu, yari yakangishije kuva muri uwo muryango Louise Mushikiwabo, uwuyobora kuva mu 2018, naramuka atorewe indi manda. U Rwanda ruhakana gufasha FRN.

Kuvamo kw'icyo gihugu cya kabiri mu kugira abavuga Igifaransa benshi cyane ku isi (miliyoni 57,3 ) nyuma y'Ubufaransa, byari kuba ari ikintu gikomeye cyane kibaye kuri OIF, isanzwe yaraciwe intege no kuba mu mwaka ushize ibihugu bitatu byo mu karere ka Sahel – Burkina Faso, Mali na Niger – byarayivuyemo.

Abakandida bane ni bo bahataniraga umwanya w'umunyamabanga mukuru wa OIF: Louise Mushikiwabo, Umunye-Congo Juliana Lumumba, akaba ari n'umukobwa wa Patrice Lumumba waharaniye ubwigenge bwa RDC, Dacian Ciolos wahoze ari Minisitiri w'intebe wa Roumanie, na Coumba Ba wahoze ari Minisitiri muri Mauritania.

Ibihugu 53 na leta by'ibinyamuryango bifite uburenganzira busesuye muri OIF (ku bihugu 90 bigize uwo muryango) byahisemo kudatora muri ayo matora yo mu ibanga, no kwiha umwaka umwe wo kubona umukandida uhuriweho kurushaho.

Taarifa Investigative Desk has reliably established from a french source that elections for the next Secretary General of the La Francophonie organisation have been postponed for one year.

“The election of the secretary-general of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (#OIF) was due to take place on Monday, November 16 in Phnom Penh, #Cambodge, but it is reportedly being postponed for a year, according to sources close to the matter,” said France24, a state-owned French holding company.

Radio France International also reported, “lacking consensus, the OIF postpones the election of the secretary-general by one year.”

The decision to delay the election for Secretary General of OIF has been welcomed differently across the Francophonie world.

Over 8,000km away from the boardroom in Phnom Penh, Kigali people are celebrating the decision as a major win against Kinshasa.

Patrick Muyaya, DRC’s Minister of Communication and Media threatened that Kinshasa would bear the consequences of a possible reappointment of the Rwandan official.

“It is precisely very, very unhealthy, once again, on the part of Mrs. Mushikiwabo, from Rwanda, to want to denounce today or to think that France, which is in its role of facilitating consensus, in accordance with the tradition established within the OIF,” Muyaya told TV5MONDE responding to comments from Mushikiwabo’s accusing France of interference in the elections.

The Chairperson of the African Union Commission (AUC), Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said, “the position of Secretary General of the International Organisation of the Francophonie (OIF) is currently the subject of a competition between African and non-African candidates. Africa must remain united to ensure an African victory. Dispersion must be avoided.”

They include Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, candidate for a third term; the former Congolese minister Juliana Lumumba, daughter of Patrice Emery Lumumba; the Mauritanian Dr Coumba Ba, minister-advisor and special envoy of President Mohamed Ould El-Ghazouani; and the former Romanian Prime Minister Dacian Cioloș.

A heavy storm earlier this month damaged tents and caused widespread flooding

The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire".

The foreign ministers warn recent floods have brought "further suffering" to the war-torn territory, which recently had its first winter storm.

The statement says 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border.

The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory.

It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".

The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs said the widespread flooding and a landslide led to a number of deaths, thousands of damaged shelters and the suspension of critical services.

The statement from the British, Australian, Canadian and Italian foreign ministers says , external : "This situation is entirely reversible - and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in."

"The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in. Dual-use items necessary for humanitarian operations and early recovery must be granted entry before it is too late."

The European Union issued a similar statement on Saturday , external , reiterating its "grave concern" over what it called the "persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis".

The EU also urged Israel to comply with international law.

The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 74,690 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israeli air strikes and other attacks have continued to take place almost every day despite the ceasefire agreed in October last year.

MN202611_1giw6rwz7sa.t:
PHNOM PENH – The contest over who should lead the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF) has exposed deep diplomatic divisions within an organization whose founding principle is to bring countries together through a shared language, cooperation and common values.

Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, whose second term as Secretary-General was due to end, has been granted a one-year extension after heads of state and government failed to reach an agreement on her successor during the summit in Phnom Penh.

The failure to resolve the leadership contest reflects a widening disagreement among member states over how the next Secretary-General should be selected. While one camp pushed for an election, others favored avoiding a vote in favor of reaching consensus on a single candidate.

The OIF recently amended its rules, making an election the preferred method of selecting the Secretary-General.

Under the new system, each member state has one vote, marking a departure from the previous practice, which prioritized consensus and gave considerable influence to major financial contributors such as Canada and France.

The stalemate followed days of intense diplomatic maneuvering, including an unsuccessful attempt by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye to persuade President Paul Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy.

According to diplomatic reporting by Africa Intelligence, a meeting convened at Faye’s initiative on the evening of November 15 failed to change Rwanda’s position, leaving member states unable to resolve the contest.

A Regional Dispute Enters the Francophonie

The strongest opposition to Mushikiwabo’s re-election came from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose government had put forward former Culture Minister Juliana Amato Lumumba as a candidate.

The Congolese government had also threatened to withdraw from the OIF should Mushikiwabo secure another term, raising the prospect of a major institutional setback for an organization already affected by the departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025.

In a last-minute change of strategy, the DRC announced its willingness to withdraw Lumumba’s candidacy and support Romania’s Dacian Cioloș, presenting the move as an attempt to find a consensus candidate and prevent the organization from becoming an extension of the Rwanda-DRC confrontation.

However, Rwanda questioned the logic of replacing an African candidate with a European one, particularly in light of an African Union decision adopted in July 2026 endorsing three African candidacies and calling on African OIF members to rally behind one of them.

“The DRC’s announced support for the Romanian candidate Dacian Cioloș, at the expense of the two other African women candidates, is a flagrant violation,” Nduhungirehe said in a statement.

France’s Influence and the Question of Consensus

France, which has considerable influence within the Francophone world as one of the organization’s largest financial contributors, found itself at the center of the diplomatic contest.

Canada, together with its associated provinces, contributes €19.4 million to the OIF, while France contributes €19.3 million.

Their financial contributions have traditionally given them considerable weight in the organization’s affairs, adding another dimension to the debate over how its leadership should be decided.

President Emmanuel Macron reportedly sought to persuade Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy, with Paris presenting its intervention as an effort to preserve the organization’s unity.

Rwanda, however, viewed the pressure as interference in a decision that should be left to member states.

The disagreement has revived questions about the extent to which former colonial powers should influence leadership decisions in an organization that brings together countries from Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.

The irony is particularly striking given Mushikiwabo’s own warning during the summit’s opening proceedings against allowing bilateral disputes to undermine the organization.

“The OIF is not a defensive alliance, and its unity does not require uniformity of positions. Members should resist turning the organization into a platform for bilateral disputes,” she said.

Its value, she added, lies in the ability of members to meet on an equal footing and turn their diversity into a source of influence and trust.

Macron similarly appealed for unity, warning against internal fractures and arguing that the organization’s strength depended on preserving cohesion among its members.

A Leadership Decision with Wider Consequences

Beyond the contest over one position, the failure to agree on the next Secretary-General raises questions about the future direction and credibility of the OIF.

The organization brings together 90 states and governments, including 53 full members, making it a significant platform for political dialogue, cultural cooperation and international engagement.

Its membership stretches well beyond countries where French is the dominant language, reflecting a broader ambition to build partnerships across continents.

The departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025 had already demonstrated how political disagreements can weaken that ambition. Losing the DRC, one of the largest French-speaking countries in the world, would further undermine the organization’s continental reach and influence.

For Mushikiwabo, the one-year extension offers continuity after eight years at the helm, but it also leaves the question of her longer-term future unresolved.

The failure to settle the leadership contest has exposed the difficulty of reconciling competing national interests under a system that is increasingly expected to rely on voting rather than consensus.

The question facing the OIF is therefore whether an organization built around linguistic and cultural ties can remain a credible multilateral platform when political rivalries among its members threaten to overshadow the common interests that brought them together.
